grounding.states: a dark, quiet room can help babies sleep
grounding.from: Mayo Clinic: A dark, quiet room can help babies sleep.

grounding.states: put a baby to bed drowsy but awake
grounding.from: It also says to put babies to bed drowsy but awake, since they sleep best when drowsy.

grounding.states: naps at the same time each day and for about the same length
grounding.from: Babies get the most out of naps if they take them at the same time each day and for about the same length of time.

grounding.states: soft lullabies before the baby gets too tired or cranky
grounding.from: soft lullabies, swaddling or massage before the baby gets too tired or cranky

grounding.states: a toddler should nap in his own bed or crib
grounding.from: It adds that a toddler at home should nap in his own bed or crib.

grounding.states: avoid lying down with the child until they fall asleep
grounding.from: avoid lying down with them until they fall asleep

grounding.states: babies sleep on their backs with no blankets or soft toys in the crib
grounding.from: Put babies to sleep on their backs, with no blankets, stuffed toys or other soft items in the crib or bassinet.

grounding.states: the search found no advice for an older child or an adult
grounding.from: These sources give no advice for an older child or an adult.

value.answer: Depends how old he is, but for a baby or toddler: put him down drowsy but still awake, at about the same time and for about the same length each day, in a dark quiet room. A soft lullaby or a calm story before he gets cranky helps. Let him fall asleep on his own, and nap in his own bed or crib. For a baby, always on the back with nothing soft in the crib. The search only turned up tips for babies and toddlers, so for an older kid or an adult I couldn't find anything I can give you.
